label: lr-8a025
summary: The network predicts churn mainly through two hinges. Customer-service calls: a typical customer's predicted risk stays at or below 3% for up to three calls and climbs to 43% at five and 95% at seven, because a direct customer-service edge and a hinge that cancels it for few calls add up. Heavy use: when the day charge and evening minutes are both high and the customer has not taken a voice-mail plan, a serial hinge opens and drives the risk towards certainty; it is open for 267 training customers, whose observed churn rate is 90.3%. An international plan raises the risk through a direct edge and a hinge (a typical customer goes from 2% to 25%); state indicators, day calls, account length and day- and evening-charge hinges shift the score by small amounts. Training AUC 0.928.

resisted: The night-calls tangle (fifteen units, three of them dead and several constant) is described, not explained: its effect on the prediction is negligible (switching it off leaves the training AUC at 0.928). Dead or constant exits inside the night-calls tangle, the day-charge hinge and the account-length gate are matched by the concept sweep to arbitrary state indicators; those matches are artefacts of exits that do not vary. The state parts are readings of the form "customers of these states get a higher or lower score" and lack a customer-level explanation; the direct state offsets probe as partial (score 0.55). The single customer with an open heavy-use gate and a voice-mail plan is a regime fitted to one row.

recheck_notes: No mismatch and no needs_review item. The unchecked free-text sentences are qualitative (mechanism descriptions without numbers) or carry only provenance-backed placeholders.
tool_bugs: (1) query_ablate's switched_off list has a header entry at index 0 (direct_edges_of_root), so edge k of the printed list is switched_off[k+1] in the stored paths; first narratives quoted the wrong edges and were corrected before the audit. (2) probe_concept's sweep matches dead or constant exits (171662_a, 191982, 241555, 4009) to an arbitrary state indicator with score 1 or null and folds that into the leaf's concept string. (3) Piping xn.py --calls into head truncated a batch of splits mid-way (SIGPIPE), not a tool bug but worth knowing.

refuted_and_fixed: single_state_boost: first read as a New Jersey boost; the probe showed the heavy-use gate's New Jersey input outweighs it, so the hypothesis now says the whole-model effect is lower risk
state_gate_pair: first read as an Alabama and Texas gate; the probe and the Alabama subgroup show it acts on Texas customers alone, Alabama never opens it
heavy_use_gate area-code term: the probe showed the area-510 shut-off of node 4534 is cancelled by direct terms (similar risk in the three area codes), stated as such

leaves.name: heavy_use_gate
leaves.best_concept: number customer service calls (exit 4823, gate on when low); area code 510 (exit 4534); state 43 (exit 82444); state 0/35 (exit 97)
leaves.why: A serial hinge on day charge and evening minutes, damped by a voice-mail plan, that drives churn risk towards certainty for heavy users; the self-probe reproduces the day-charge threshold and its shift with a voice-mail plan, and its main exit also carries the few-customer-service-calls hinge.

leaves.name: night_calls_tangle
leaves.best_concept: total night calls (exit 15132); area code 510 / state 16 (exit 8508); constant exit matched to state 0
leaves.why: Live terms read night calls and an area-510 indicator, but with negligible output weight and dead or constant links; described rather than explained.

leaves.name: day_charge_hinge
leaves.why: A hinge that lowers the score as daytime spending rises above a threshold; the sweep confirms the onset and the offset against the heavy-use gate.

leaves.name: state_gate_pair
leaves.why: A Texas indicator lowering the score slightly; the Alabama input never opens the exit, confirmed on every Alabama row.

leaves.name: day_calls
leaves.why: More day calls raise the score through a two-unit hinge; the sweep confirms the onset and rise.

leaves.name: intl_plan_hinge
leaves.why: On for every international-plan holder and for none of the others, raising their score; confirmed by subgroup counts and the probe.

leaves.name: eve_charge_hinge
leaves.best_concept: total eve minutes (same column as total eve charge after z-scoring)
leaves.why: Heavier evening spending above the typical value lowers the score slightly; the sweep confirms the onset.

leaves.name: account_length_gate
leaves.why: Longer accounts raise the score slightly, shut for Nebraska customers; the sweep and the Nebraska subgroup confirm both.

leaves.name: state_gates_lower
leaves.why: State indicators (Hawaii, Washington DC, Nebraska, Virginia, Connecticut, Delaware, Oklahoma) that lower the score; the probe confirms each state's shift.

leaves.name: state_gates_raise
leaves.why: State indicators (Maine, Minnesota, Michigan, New York, Tennessee) that raise the score, mostly Maine and Minnesota; the probe confirms.

leaves.name: single_state_boost
leaves.why: A New Jersey indicator that raises the score through this part, outweighed in the whole model by the heavy-use gate's New Jersey term; confirmed by the probe.

leaves.name: direct_usage_terms
leaves.why: The linear direct terms, led by customer-service calls and an international plan; the probe confirms the international-plan shift and the linear rise with calls.

leaves.name: direct_state_offsets
leaves.why: Linear per-state offsets; the largest (Ohio) is cancelled inside the heavy-use gate, and the offsets have no reading beyond state membership.

overall_function: The network scores churn mainly from customer-service calls and heavy phone use. Customer-service calls act as a hinge: the score is flat for a few calls and rises steeply beyond about three, built from a linear direct edge and a hinge that cancels it at low counts. Combined day charge and evening minutes (with a little night and international use) open a serial hinge that drives the predicted risk towards certainty for heavy users; a voice-mail plan raises the threshold, and separate small hinges on day charge and evening charge pull slightly the other way. An international plan raises the risk (direct edge plus a hinge), more international calls and a voice-mail plan lower it directly, and many states and account length shift the score by small amounts; the area code's terms largely cancel. The model ignores day minutes, night charge and international charge (it uses their twin columns), evening calls, voice-mail message counts, and about a third of the states.
clinical_terms: In customer terms: customers who have called customer service four or more times, and customers with heavy daytime plus evening usage who have not taken a voice-mail plan, are predicted to churn at high rates; an international plan raises the predicted risk, while a voice-mail plan and more international calls lower it. The joint effect is a usage threshold: the heavy-use gate detects customers whose combined day and evening use exceeds a level that a voice-mail plan pushes higher. Location (state) adds small up or down offsets; area code has almost no net effect.
stuck: Little: the main friction was tool behaviour (switched_off index offset, concept sweep matching constant exits to arbitrary states). The night-calls tangle stays one leaf because its dead and constant links tie its units together; splitting it would need a cascade of hidden and input splits for a part with negligible effect.
